## Today's question {.ml-question-slide}

<div class="ml-question">
<span>WE CAN ALREADY PREDICT</span>
<b>global mean · user mean · item mean</b>
<p>How do we move from hand-designed averages to a general way of learning prediction rules from data?</p>
</div>

<div class="question-bridge">
<div><span>BEFORE</span><b>Choose a formula</b><p>Then calculate its averages from the training triples.</p></div>
<i>→</i>
<div><span>TODAY</span><b>Choose a model family</b><p>Then learn its parameters from examples.</p></div>
<i>→</i>
<div><span>THE REAL CHALLENGE</span><b>Generalize</b><p>Work well on ratings the model has never seen.</p></div>
</div>

## Four questions decode every estimator {.detail-slide .components-slide}

<div class="four-components">
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><span>1 · MODEL</span><b>$f_{\theta,h}(x)$</b><p>What family of prediction rules can this estimator represent?</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><span>2 · LEARNED PARAMETERS</span><b>$\theta$</b><p>What quantities will <code>fit</code> learn from the training data?</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><span>3 · HYPERPARAMETERS</span><b>$h$</b><p>What choices are fixed before <code>fit</code> and control the model or fitting rule?</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="4"><span>4 · LOSS / CRITERION</span><b>$L(y,\widehat y)$</b><p>What does the fitting procedure regard as a better solution?</p></div>
</div>

<div class="component-equation fragment fade-in" data-fragment-index="5">
<div class="component-flow">
<div><span>BEFORE FIT</span><b>choose settings</b>$$h$$</div>
<i>→</i>
<div><span>DURING FIT</span><b>learn from training data</b>$$\widehat\theta$$<small>guided by the loss or fitting criterion</small></div>
<i>→</i>
<div><span>AFTER FIT</span><b>predict new rows</b>$$\widehat y=f_{\widehat\theta,h}(x_{\mathrm{new}})$$</div>
</div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
[Teaching]
- Establish this as the reusable reading template for the course. Every time a new estimator appears, ask the same four questions before studying its code.
- “Loss / criterion” is deliberately broad. Some estimators minimize an explicit loss; others use a direct fitting rule. The visible flow applies to both.
- Data remain essential: $X$ supplies inputs and $y$ supplies training answers. The previous two slides established that shared data format; these four questions describe the estimator itself.
:::

## Linear regression combines the features {.detail-slide .linear-model-slide}

<div class="linear-equation">
$$f_{\theta}(x)=\theta_0+\sum_{j=1}^{8}\theta_j x_j$$
</div>

<div class="coefficient-reading">
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><span>$\theta_0$</span><b>intercept</b><p>the model's reference level</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><span>$\theta_j$</span><b>coefficient</b><p>how prediction changes with feature $j$, holding others fixed</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><span>$\widehat y$</span><b>prediction</b><p>a weighted sum calculated for one row</p></div>
</div>

<p class="ml-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="4">Here each row has eight housing features. A choice of nine numbers $\theta_0,\ldots,\theta_8$ gives one prediction rule.</p>

## Least squares fits the housing coefficients {.detail-slide .lr-objective-slide}

<div class="lr-objective">
<span>ONE TRAINING BLOCK GROUP</span>
$$e_k(\theta)=y_k-f_\theta(x_k), \qquad \ell_k(\theta)=e_k(\theta)^2$$
<span>ALL TRAINING BLOCK GROUPS</span>
$$\widehat\theta=\arg\min_{\theta\in\mathbb R^9}
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(y_k-f_\theta(x_k)\right)^2$$
</div>

<div class="lr-argmin-reading">
<p><b>minimum</b> is the smallest training loss.</p>
<p><b>arg minimum</b> is the coefficient vector that achieves it.</p>
</div>

<p class="ml-takeaway">Training chooses the intercept and eight coefficients that minimize the squared errors on the training rows.</p>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- Ordinary least squares fitting criterion: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression.html.

[Teaching]
- The average and the sum have the same minimizer. The averaging factor does not change the learned coefficients.
- After the estimator interface, link the mathematical result $\widehat\theta$ to the fitted Python attributes.
:::

## Training and test answer different questions {.detail-slide .roles-slide}

<div class="role-contrast">
<div class="train-role">
<span>TRAINING SET</span>
<b>How should the model fit?</b>
<ul>
<li><code>X_train</code> and <code>y_train</code> are available</li>
<li>estimates parameters</li>
<li>may be reused during fitting</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="test-role">
<span>TEST INPUT AND LABEL</span>
<b>What may the model see?</b>
<ul>
<li><code>X_test</code> is available for prediction</li>
<li><code>y_test</code> does not estimate parameters</li>
<li><code>y_test</code> is opened only for final evaluation</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

<p class="ml-takeaway"><b>Generalization</b> is performance on new examples drawn from the task we care about.</p>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- The train/test distinction follows scikit-learn’s model-selection guidance: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/model_selection.html.
:::

## From model to scikit-learn estimator {.section-break .estimator-section}

<div class="section-number">03</div>
<img class="section-crest" src="../Lec-overview/figs/cu_logo.webp" alt="CUHK emblem">

## One contract for every prediction model {.detail-slide .estimator-contract-slide}

<div class="estimator-contract" role="img" aria-label="An estimator is constructed, fitted on training inputs and targets, then used to predict new inputs">
<div class="contract-stage"><span>CONSTRUCT</span><b><code>model = Estimator(...)</code></b><p>Choose the model and its settings.</p></div>
<i class="fragment" data-fragment-index="1"><code>model.fit(X, y)</code></i>
<div class="contract-stage fitted-stage fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><span>LEARN</span><b>fitted estimator</b><p>Store patterns learned from the training data.</p></div>
<i class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2"><code>model.predict(X_new)</code></i>
<div class="contract-stage prediction-stage fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><span>APPLY</span><b>prediction vector</b><p>Return one prediction for each new row.</p></div>
</div>

<div class="contract-equivalence fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3">
<code>LinearRegression()</code><code>KNeighborsRegressor()</code><code>YourRegressor()</code><b>can share the same interface</b>
</div>

<p class="ml-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="4">The contract specifies <b>how we use a model</b>. Each estimator supplies its own learning and prediction rules.</p>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- Estimator, predictor, and regressor interfaces: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/developers/develop.html.
:::

## Class, estimator, and fitted estimator {.detail-slide .class-estimator-slide}

<div class="class-estimator-map" role="img" aria-label="A Python class defines the structure, construction creates an unfitted estimator instance, and fit updates that same instance with learned attributes">
<div class="class-blueprint">
<span>PYTHON CLASS</span>
<b><code>LinearRegression</code></b>
<pre>__init__(settings)
fit(X, y)
predict(X_new)</pre>
<p>Defines settings and methods; <code>fit</code> later stores learned attributes.</p>
</div>

<div class="class-map-step fragment" data-fragment-index="1"><code>call the class</code><b>creates</b></div>

<div class="estimator-instance fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1">
<span>ESTIMATOR INSTANCE</span>
<b><code>model = LinearRegression(<br>fit_intercept=True)</code></b>
<div class="instance-state"><i>available now</i><code>fit_intercept</code></div>
<div class="instance-state missing-state"><i>not learned yet</i><code>coef_</code></div>
<p>A configured Python object, ready to receive data.</p>
</div>

<div class="class-map-step fit-map-step fragment" data-fragment-index="2"><code>model.fit(X, y)</code><b>updates</b></div>

<div class="estimator-instance fitted-instance fragment fade-left" data-fragment-index="2">
<span>FITTED ESTIMATOR</span>
<b><code>model</code></b>
<div class="instance-state"><i>configuration</i><code>fit_intercept</code></div>
<div class="instance-state learned-state fragment" data-fragment-index="3"><i>learned from data</i><code>coef_</code></div>
<div class="instance-state learned-state fragment" data-fragment-index="3"><i>learned from data</i><code>intercept_</code></div>
<p>The same object now contains fitted state.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="identity-rule fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="4"><code>model.fit(X, y) is model</code><b><code>True</code></b><span><code>fit</code> conventionally returns <code>self</code>.</span></div>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- Estimators are objects that implement fit; fit returns self: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/developers/develop.html.
- Fitted public attributes use a trailing underscore: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/developers/develop.html#estimated-attributes.

[Teaching]
- This slide introduces the Python object before the next slides use it on California housing.
:::

## Fit and predict with California housing {.detail-slide .linear-estimator-slide .code-slide}

:::: {.columns .vcenter}
::: {.column width="56%"}
~~~python
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

model = LinearRegression(fit_intercept=True)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

model.coef_        # eight learned coefficients
model.intercept_   # learned intercept

y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
~~~
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
<div class="linear-example-reading">
<p><span><code>fit_intercept</code></span><b>chosen before fitting</b><em>Controls whether the model includes $\theta_0$.</em></p>
<p><span><code>coef_</code>, <code>intercept_</code></span><b>learned during <code>fit</code></b><em>The trailing underscore marks fitted attributes.</em></p>
<p><span><code>y_pred</code></span><b>one value per test row</b><em><code>predict</code> sees eight features and no target.</em></p>
</div>
:::
::::

<p class="ml-takeaway"><code>model</code> is one object: <code>fit</code> stores the learned values; <code>predict</code> applies them to new block groups.</p>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- LinearRegression fit, predict, and fitted attributes: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression.html.

[Teaching]
- Keep the housing dataset on screen as the context. The notebook's small array exercise gives students a separate chance to calculate the coefficients by hand.
:::

## Many errors become one RMSE {.detail-slide .rmse-process-slide}

<p class="rmse-context">Illustrative test rows; house values in units of $100,000</p>

<div class="rmse-process">
<div class="rmse-vector">
<span>TRUE</span><b>$y$</b><em>2.4</em><em>1.8</em><em>3.2</em><em>2.6</em>
</div>
<div class="rmse-op fragment" data-fragment-index="1">−</div>
<div class="rmse-vector fragment" data-fragment-index="1">
<span>PREDICTED</span><b>$\widehat y$</b><em>2.1</em><em>2.0</em><em>2.7</em><em>2.8</em>
</div>
<div class="rmse-op fragment" data-fragment-index="2">→</div>
<div class="rmse-vector error-vector fragment" data-fragment-index="2">
<span>ERROR</span><b>$e$</b><em>0.3</em><em>−0.2</em><em>0.5</em><em>−0.2</em>
</div>
</div>

<div class="rmse-steps">
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><span>01</span><b>square</b><p>0.09, 0.04, 0.25, 0.04</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="4"><span>02</span><b>average</b><p>$(0.42)/4=0.105$</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up answer" data-fragment-index="5"><span>03</span><b>square root</b><p>$\mathrm{RMSE}=0.324$</p></div>
</div>

<p class="ml-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="6"><code>root_mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred)</code> calculates RMSE from the true and predicted test values.</p>

## `GlobalMeanRS`: specify before coding {.detail-slide .reading-template-slide}

<div class="baseline-question-grid">
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><span>MODEL</span><b>$f_c(u,i)=c$</b><p>The family contains every constant prediction rule.</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><span>HYPERPARAMETERS</span><b>none</b><p>No setting is chosen before fitting.</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><span>LOSS / CRITERION</span><b>$J(c)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(r_j-c)^2$</b><p>$r_1,\ldots,r_n$ are the training ratings. Compare constants by total squared error.</p></div>
</div>

<div class="baseline-optimization fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="4">
<span>FIT · OPTIMIZE</span>
<div class="mean-fit-steps">
<div><small>MINIMIZE THE LOSS</small>$$\widehat\mu=\arg\min_{c\in\mathbb R}J(c)$$</div>
<i>→</i>
<div><small>THE FITTED VALUE</small>$$\widehat\mu=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}r_j$$</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="baseline-learned fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="5"><span>LEARNED PARAMETER AFTER <code>fit</code></span><b>$\widehat\mu$</b><p>stored as <code>global_mean_</code> · <code>predict</code> returns it once per new row</p></div>

::: {.notes}
[Teaching]
- Reveal the learned parameter only after the optimization step.
- The mean is not an arbitrary summary: it is the minimizer of squared loss among constant predictions.
:::

## Now implement `GlobalMeanRS` {.detail-slide .global-estimator-slide .code-slide}

:::: {.columns .vcenter}
::: {.column width="61%"}
~~~python
import numpy as np
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin
from sklearn.utils.validation import check_is_fitted

class GlobalMeanRS(RegressorMixin, BaseEstimator):
    def fit(self, X, y):
        self.global_mean_ = np.asarray(y).mean()
        return self

    def predict(self, X):
        check_is_fitted(self, "global_mean_")
        return np.full(len(X), self.global_mean_)
~~~
:::

::: {.column width="35%"}
<div class="global-estimator-reading">
<p class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><span>FIT</span><b>one learned value</b><em><code>global_mean_</code> comes from <code>y</code>.</em></p>
<p class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><span>PREDICT</span><b>one value per row</b><em><code>X</code> determines only how many predictions to return.</em></p>
<p class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><span>CHECK</span><b>fit must happen first</b><em>Otherwise scikit-learn raises <code>NotFittedError</code>.</em></p>
</div>
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- Class structure follows the custom-estimator conventions in https://scikit-learn.org/stable/developers/develop.html.
- Fitted-state validation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.utils.validation.check_is_fitted.html.
:::

## `UserMeanRS`: specify before coding {.detail-slide .reading-template-slide}

<div class="baseline-question-grid">
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><span>MODEL</span><b>$f_{\mathbf a}(u,i)=a_u$</b><p>One candidate constant per user; use the global rule for an unseen user.</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><span>HYPERPARAMETERS</span><b>none</b><p>The grouping and fallback rule are fixed in this definition.</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><span>LOSS / CRITERION</span><b>$J_u(c)=\sum_{i\in I_u}(r_{ui}-c)^2$</b><p>$I_u$ contains items rated by user $u$ in training.</p></div>
</div>

<div class="baseline-optimization fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="4">
<span>FIT · EACH USER $u$</span>
<div class="mean-fit-steps">
<div><small>MINIMIZE USER LOSS</small>$$\widehat a_u=\arg\min_{c\in\mathbb R}J_u(c)$$</div>
<i>→</i>
<div><small>USER'S RATING MEAN</small>$$\widehat a_u=\frac{1}{|I_u|}\sum_{i\in I_u}r_{ui}$$</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="baseline-learned fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="5"><span>LEARNED PARAMETERS AFTER <code>fit</code></span><b>$\widehat\mu,\{\widehat a_u\}$</b><p>stored as <code>global_mean_</code> and <code>user_means_</code> · retrieve by user ID</p></div>

::: {.notes}
[Teaching]
- Reveal the learned parameters only after showing the per-user optimization.
- The user-mean model has many learned parameters even though it has no hyperparameters.
- The item ID remains in the input pair, but this prediction rule does not use it.
:::

## User mean learns a lookup vector {.detail-slide .user-mean-fit-slide}

<div class="user-mean-learning">
<div class="user-rating-groups">
<span>GROUP TRAINING RATINGS BY USER</span>
<div class="user-group fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><b>$u_0$</b><i>4</i><i>2</i><i>3</i><strong>mean = 3.0</strong></div>
<div class="user-group fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><b>$u_1$</b><i>5</i><i>4</i><i>3</i><strong>mean = 4.0</strong></div>
<div class="user-group sparse-group fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><b>$u_2$</b><i>2</i><strong>mean = 2.0</strong></div>
</div>
<i class="fragment" data-fragment-index="4">store</i>
<div class="user-mean-state fragment fade-left" data-fragment-index="4">
<span>FITTED ATTRIBUTES</span>
<pre>global_mean_ = 3.3

user ID        0    1    2
user_means_ = [3.0, 4.0, 2.0]</pre>
<p>Only a user absent from training uses <code>global_mean_</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>

<p class="ml-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="5">Every observed user receives a mean. The global mean handles users absent from training.</p>

::: {.notes}
[Teaching]
- The numbers are a small schematic example. The global mean is rounded for display.
- This is the same user-mean rule used in the baseline lecture. The fallback handles only users absent from training.
:::

## Implement `UserMeanRS`: `fit` {.detail-slide .user-estimator-slide .code-slide}

:::: {.columns .vcenter}
::: {.column width="66%"}
~~~python
class UserMeanRS(RegressorMixin, BaseEstimator):
    def fit(self, X, y):
        X, y = np.asarray(X), np.asarray(y)
        users = X[:, 0].astype(int)
        self.global_mean_ = y.mean()
        self.user_means_ = np.full(
            users.max() + 1, self.global_mean_
        )

        for user in set(users):
            ratings = y[users == user]
            self.user_means_[user] = ratings.mean()
        return self
~~~
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
<div class="user-estimator-reading">
<p><span><code>global_mean_</code></span><b>fallback learned by <code>fit</code></b></p>
<p><span><code>user_means_</code></span><b>NumPy lookup vector learned by <code>fit</code></b></p>
<p><span><code>users == user</code></span><b>select that user's ratings</b></p>
</div>
:::
::::

<p class="source-line">Input: a two-column array with nonnegative user ID in column 0.</p>

## Complete `UserMeanRS`: `predict` {.detail-slide .user-estimator-slide .code-slide}

:::: {.columns .vcenter}
::: {.column width="66%"}
~~~python
def predict(self, X):
    check_is_fitted(
        self, ["global_mean_", "user_means_"]
    )
    users = np.asarray(X)[:, 0].astype(int)
    y_pred = np.full(len(users), self.global_mean_)

    valid = (users >= 0) & (users < len(self.user_means_))
    y_pred[valid] = self.user_means_[users[valid]]
    return y_pred
~~~
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
<div class="user-estimator-reading">
<p><span><code>check_is_fitted</code></span><b>require <code>fit</code> first</b></p>
<p><span><code>y_pred</code></span><b>start every row at the global mean</b></p>
<p><span><code>valid</code></span><b>which user IDs have a safe lookup index?</b></p>
<p><span><code>y_pred[valid]</code></span><b>replace fallback with learned user means</b></p>
</div>
:::
::::

<p class="source-line">Add this method inside the `UserMeanRS` class from the previous slide.</p>

## `ItemMeanRS`: transfer the same template {.detail-slide .reading-template-slide}

<div class="baseline-question-grid">
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><span>MODEL</span><b>$f_{\mathbf b}(u,i)=b_i$</b><p>One candidate constant per item; use the global rule for an unseen item.</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><span>HYPERPARAMETERS</span><b>none</b><p>The grouping and fallback rule are fixed in this definition.</p></div>
<div class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><span>LOSS / CRITERION</span><b>$J_i(c)=\sum_{u\in U_i}(r_{ui}-c)^2$</b><p>$U_i$ contains users who rated item $i$ in training.</p></div>
</div>

<div class="baseline-optimization fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="4">
<span>FIT · EACH ITEM $i$</span>
<div class="mean-fit-steps">
<div><small>MINIMIZE ITEM LOSS</small>$$\widehat b_i=\arg\min_{c\in\mathbb R}J_i(c)$$</div>
<i>→</i>
<div><small>ITEM'S RATING MEAN</small>$$\widehat b_i=\frac{1}{|U_i|}\sum_{u\in U_i}r_{ui}$$</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="baseline-learned fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="5"><span>LEARNED PARAMETERS AFTER <code>fit</code></span><b>$\widehat\mu,\{\widehat b_i\}$</b><p>stored as <code>global_mean_</code> and <code>item_means_</code> · retrieve by item ID</p></div>

::: {.notes}
[Teaching]
- Reveal the learned parameters only after showing the per-item optimization.
- Ask what changed from UserMeanRS: the template is identical; only the grouping index changes.
- [Notebook pause 3] Open Sections 6–9 of `STAT3009_ML_I.ipynb`. Implement `GlobalMeanRS` and `UserMeanRS`, compare their predictions, then let students complete `ItemMeanRS`.
:::

## One workflow can use every estimator {.detail-slide .shared-interface-slide .code-slide}

:::: {.columns .vcenter}
::: {.column width="58%"}
~~~python
models = [
    GlobalMeanRS(),
    UserMeanRS(),
]

for model in models:
    fitted_model = model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    y_pred = fitted_model.predict(X_new)

    print(type(model).__name__, y_pred.shape)
~~~
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
<div class="interface-output">
<span>OUTPUT · $m$ = NUMBER OF ROWS IN <code>X_new</code></span>
<pre>GlobalMeanRS  (m,)
UserMeanRS    (m,)</pre>
</div>

<div class="interface-payoff">
<p class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1"><b>Same inputs</b><span><code>X_train</code>, <code>y_train</code>, <code>X_new</code></span></p>
<p class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="2"><b>Same methods</b><span><code>fit</code> and <code>predict</code></span></p>
<p class="fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="3"><b>Same output contract</b><span>one prediction per new row</span></p>
</div>
:::
::::

<p class="ml-takeaway fragment" data-fragment-index="4">Model-specific logic stays inside each class. Workflow code depends only on the shared estimator interface.</p>

::: {.notes}
[Teaching]
- This is the practical payoff of the estimator contract. The loop does not need an `if` statement for each model type.
- `m` denotes the number of rows in `X_new`. The two models produce different values but obey the same output shape.
:::
